描述_ZN: The page of "Yinzhen's book of cultivation and weaving - mowing", Qing Dynasty, on silk with color, 39.4 cm in length and 32.7 cm in width.    This is one of the openings of the Atlas of Tilling and Weaving. It depicts Yinzhen (Prince Yong), dressed as a farmer in a wheat field, leading the harvest. The painting is well-drawn, elegantly colored, and the figures are vivid and evocative, depicting the scene of laborers hard at work.    Originating from the Southern Song Dynasty, it is a series of detailed records of farming and sericulture for the purpose of advising farming and mulberry in ancient China. Because of its "drawing to exhaust its situation, poetry to exhaust its feelings", the image vividly and delicately depicts the scene of cultivation and silkworm weaving and the detailed production process, thus playing a huge role in popularizing the knowledge of agricultural production, promoting farming techniques and facilitating the development of social productivity, and itself has become an extremely valuable artistic treasure.    The Song Dynasty's book of "Plowing and Weaving" consists of 21 pictures of plowing and 24 pictures of weaving. Qing Kangxi 28 (1689), the Kangxi emperor when the southern tour to view the map, emotionally, so ordered the inner court Jiao Bingzhen according to its original intention to redraw the "cultivation and weaving" book, as 23 plowing map, weaving map 23.    Yongzheng plowing and weaving" book is the Yongzheng emperor before ascending to the throne to the Kangxi years engraved and printed "plowing and weaving" as a blueprint, the content and specifications after Jiao's book, by the Qing court painter carefully drawn. The difference is that the main characters in Yinzhen plowing and weaving diagram such as farmers, sericulture women, etc. are the portraits of Yinzhen and his Fujin, which is only seen in the plowing and weaving diagram in successive generations. The picture survives 52 pages, of which 6 pages are undrafted derivative pages, and the remaining 46 pages are 23 pages each of plowing and weaving, each with a poem inscribed in Yinzhen's own handwriting and inscribed with two seals, "Prince Yong Bao" and "Broken Dust Jushi". According to the characteristics of the painting method, this album probably came from the hand of Chen Mei, the court painter at that time.
